primary_diagnosis_treated: Obesity-driven Metabolic Syndrome (including hypertension, prediabetes, dyslipidaemia, obesity, obstructive sleep apnoea)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg PO once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5 mg then 10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — titrate over 4‑6 weeks, then review annually
medications.purpose: Control stage 2 hypertension to target <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends an ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive in metabolic syndrome

medications.duration: Add if BP remains >140/90 mmHg after 6 weeks of maximally tolerated ramipril; then lifelong
medications.purpose: Second‑line antihypertensive to achieve BP target
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises adding a CCB when BP not at target on ACE‑I alone

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile review at 3 months then annually
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 recommends statin therapy for adults with QRISK ≥10 % or metabolic‑syndrome components

medications.dose: 500 mg PO once daily with evening meal, increase by 500 mg weekly to 1000 mg twice daily (max 2 g/day)
medications.purpose: Prevent progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 advises metformin for high‑risk prediabetes when lifestyle alone is insufficient

medications.dose: 120 mg PO three times daily with each main meal containing fat
medications.duration: 12 months then reassess weight and metabolic parameters
medications.purpose: Weight loss in obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²) to improve metabolic syndrome components
medications.nice_justification: NICE PH46 recommends orlistat for BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² or ≥ 28 kg/m² with comorbidities

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential additive hypotensive effect causing dizziness or orthostatic fall
interactions_checked.action: Advise patient to rise slowly, monitor BP after first dose, and report symptomatic hypotension

contraindications.reason: eGFR unknown; contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (risk of lactic acidosis)
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR <30, use lifestyle intervention alone or consider a DPP‑4 inhibitor

contraindications.reason: eGFR and serum potassium unknown; ACE‑I contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² or K⁺ >5.0 mmol/L
contraindications.alternative: If ACE‑I unsuitable, use an ARB such as losartan

contraindications.reason: Liver function tests not available; contraindicated in active liver disease or ALT >3× ULN
contraindications.alternative: If liver disease present, consider pravastatin or avoid statin until LFTs normal

contraindications.reason: Chronic malabsorption or cholestasis not documented; contraindicated in these conditions
contraindications.alternative: Consider GLP‑1 RA (e.g., semaglutide) for weight loss if malabsorption present

assumptions_warnings: eGFR, serum creatinine and potassium are not provided – assumed normal for initiating ACE‑I and metformin; labs must be obtained before starting.
Baseline liver function tests are missing – required before starting atorvastatin.
Fasting lipid profile and QRISK score are not available – assumed QRISK ≥10 % given hypertension, obesity and prediabetes; calculate QRISK once age, sex and smoking status are known.
BMI and waist circumference not recorded – assumed BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² for obesity drug eligibility; measure at next visit.
Cause of anaemia not established – iron studies required before prescribing ferrous sulfate.
OSA status is untreated – referral for sleep study/CPAP is recommended per NICE CG188.
Allergy history to ACE‑I, statin or orlistat not documented – verify before prescribing.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrate to 10 mg) for hypertension, add amlodipine 5 mg if target BP not achieved, initiate atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for primary CVD prevention, begin metformin 500 mg daily (titrate to 1 g BID) to prevent diabetes, and offer orlistat 120 mg TID for weight loss. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, LFTs, BP, HbA1c and lipids according to NICE schedules, and arrange CPAP referral for obstructive sleep apnoea. Ensure all baseline labs are obtained and review diphenhydramine use due to potential sedation and hypotensive synergy.
